X-13ARIMA seasonal adjustment (JDemetra+ v3)

Source: R/models.R
X13.Rd

Defines an X-13ARIMA model to be used inside fabletools::model(). The model is estimated with rjd3x13::jx13() and the Java result is kept in the fitted model, so that all JDemetra+ indicators can be extracted afterwards (see jd3_indicator()).

Usage

X13(
  formula,
  spec = c("rsa4", "rsa0", "rsa1", "rsa2c", "rsa3", "rsa5c"),
  context = NULL,
  ref_spec = spec,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

Model formula: the name of the variable to adjust (y), or y ~ specials (see jd3_specials).

spec

Base specification: a character name (see rjd3x13::x13_spec() for the available names; the default is the first one) or a specification object from rjd3x13::x13_spec(). The specials of the formula are applied to it.

context

A modelling context created with rjd3toolkit::modelling_context() (e.g. for custom calendars), or NULL.

ref_spec

Reference specification stored in the model: it is the reference of the refresh policies used by refit() and stream(). Defaults to spec, that is the specification before its modification by the specials.

...

Currently unused.

Value

A model definition that can be passed to fabletools::model(). Once fitted, the mable column contains a jd3_model object. Use components() to get the decomposition as a dable (columns trend, seasonal, irregular and season_adjust).

Details

The specification can be set in two (combinable) ways:

  1. Ex ante, with the spec argument: a name or a specification object created with rjd3x13::x13_spec() and modified with the set_*() functions of rjd3toolkit.

  2. In the formula, with specials such as transform() or xreg() (see jd3_specials). This is the only way to use regressors that are columns of the tsibble.

Specials override the base spec.

See also

TRAMOSEATS(), REGARIMA(), jd3_specials, jd3_model_methods, jd3_indicator(), jd3_dictionary()

Examples

y <- tsibble::as_tsibble(AirPassengers)

# Default specification
mb <- model(y, x13 = X13(value))
components(mb)
#> # A dable: 144 x 7 [1M]
#> # Key:     .model [1]
#> # :        value = trend * seasonal * irregular
#>    .model    index value trend seasonal irregular season_adjust
#>    <chr>     <mth> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>         <dbl>
#>  1 x13    1949 Jan   112  122.    0.920     0.996          122.
#>  2 x13    1949 Feb   118  124.    0.948     1.00           125.
#>  3 x13    1949 Mar   132  126.    1.05      0.994          125.
#>  4 x13    1949 Apr   129  128.    1.00      1.01           129.
#>  5 x13    1949 May   121  128.    0.939     1.01           129.
#>  6 x13    1949 Jun   135  127.    1.07      0.998          127.
#>  7 x13    1949 Jul   148  126.    1.19      0.988          125.
#>  8 x13    1949 Aug   148  126.    1.17      0.999          126.
#>  9 x13    1949 Sep   136  127.    1.07      1.00           128.
#> 10 x13    1949 Oct   119  128.    0.925     1.00           129.
#> # ℹ 134 more rows

# Specification created ex ante with rjd3toolkit
my_spec <- rjd3x13::x13_spec("rsa3")
my_spec <- rjd3toolkit::set_transform(my_spec, fun = "Log")
mb <- model(y, x13 = X13(value, spec = my_spec))

# Specification set in the formula with specials
mb <- model(
  y,
  x13 = X13(value ~ transform(fun = "Log") +
              outlier(outliers.type = c("AO", "LS")))
)

# Regressor taken from a column of the tsibble
y$shock <- as.numeric(y$index == tsibble::yearmonth("1955 Jan"))
mb <- model(y, x13 = X13(value ~ xreg(shock, regeffect = "Series")))
#> Warning: 1 error encountered for x13
#> [1] unused argument (effect = x$regeffect)
